article_content: A staggering nine out of ten employees at the Care Quality Commission (CQC) believe there is a pervasive culture of bullying within the organization, according to a recent report. The CQC, which has been heavily criticized for failing to detect several healthcare scandals, saw 92% of its staff report feelings of being bullied or harassed. Employees described a 'systemic bullying' environment where many were too afraid to speak up, even under the promise of anonymity, fearing that doing so could worsen their situation or lead to punishment. The CQC has been blamed for not identifying systematic neglect at Mid Staffs and Morecambe Bay trusts. Staff members responsible for inspecting hospitals for abuse and neglect reported feeling 'overwhelmed' by their workload, caught in a cycle of blame, and 'broken' by their managers' behavior. The report, which cost £54,000, was commissioned by the CQC in December after the new chairman, David Behan, called the bullying allegations 'shocking and unacceptable'. This revelation comes just a month after the CQC was criticized for covering up its failure to spot problems at Morecambe Bay hospitals, where up to 16 babies died due to neglect. In an attempt to protect their reputations, CQC bosses ordered the destruction of a damning document that highlighted flaws in their inspection process. The CQC has also been accused of overlooking the horrific abuse of disabled patients at Winterbourne View hospital. Former inspectors who exposed these catastrophic failings claimed they were bullied, harassed, and silenced to prevent them from criticizing the regulator. Kay Sheldon, a CQC board member, attempted to warn about the dangers to patients due to the organization's poor performance. However, Dame Jo Williams, the chairman at the time, allegedly used public funds to commission a mental health assessment of Ms. Sheldon and tried to suspend her. Ms. Sheldon welcomed the report's findings, tweeting: 'Bullying culture in organization was one of the main concerns I raised in 2011. Completely refuted by board & exec team.' In total, 92% of the 236 CQC staff who provided evidence felt they had been bullied or harassed. The report's authors, from the consultancy firm People Opportunities, believe the issue affects the entire organization. Matthew Sinclair of the TaxPayers' Alliance stated: 'The CQC appears to have let down not only the patients it was supposed to protect but also its own staff. No wonder it was unable to expose failings within the NHS when it presided over its own culture of bullying and poor management.' CQC chief executive David Behan expressed gratitude to the staff who shared their experiences, stating that their honesty was crucial in identifying necessary improvements. In related news, the largest hospital in Wales has been labeled 'dangerous' in a damning report, with an MP comparing it to the 2010 scandal at the Mid Staffs Trust. The report from the Royal College of Surgeons claimed that patients at the University Hospital of Wales in Cardiff died while waiting for operations, and the A&E department was struggling to meet demand. The report warned: 'Patients are clearly coming to harm. In cardiac surgery we heard patients are regularly dying on the waiting list.' Doctors perceived that operations were being cut to save money. Labour MP Ann Clwyd, whose husband died at the hospital, said: 'To hear from the RCS through a leaked report that departments are dangerous, with patients dying regularly, that is horrifying – and particularly because we didn’t know about it. The situation sounds to me similar to the Mid Staffs situation. This is the Welsh Mid Staffs moment.' Health board chief Adam Cairns apologized for the hospital's poor performance but refused calls for his resignation.

article_content: Australians residing in major cities will face significant increases in their annual gas bills as prices surge. A report from the Grattan Institute indicates that the average household gas bill in most major centers will rise by hundreds of dollars annually. In Melbourne, the price increase is expected to be particularly severe, potentially reaching $435 per year, largely due to Australia's strong position in the emerging liquefied natural gas (LNG) export industry. Capital city residents are bracing for substantial hikes in their gas bills. Melbourne, in particular, will be hardest hit, with average household costs potentially rising by as much as $435 annually. According to Tony Wood, the energy program director at the Grattan Institute, the growth of the LNG export industry, valued at around $60 billion annually, will drive up domestic prices as Australians compete internationally for gas supplies. Wood also warns that Australia may struggle to meet its 2020 emissions reduction targets, as the rise in gas prices leads to increased coal usage for electricity generation. In Melbourne, where 90% of homes rely on gas for cooking, hot water, and heating, the average bill could increase by up to $435 annually. Residents in Sydney and Adelaide can expect increases of over $200, while Brisbane is likely to be less affected due to lower gas consumption. The report highlights that gas producers have been constructing LNG facilities, primarily in Queensland, since 2010, with exports expected to begin this year. By 2018, the combined output from the east coast and Western Australia could make Australia the world's largest gas exporter, valued at over $60 billion annually. However, this will come at the cost of higher domestic gas prices, as Australia competes with international markets. Wood advises against government intervention through subsidies, arguing that such measures would add costs without increasing supply, ultimately harming everyone in the long run. For low gas users, such as those with a gas cooktop or small hot water system, the increase in average bills could be limited to less than $50 annually.

PUBLISHED: 10:31 EST, 1 October 2013 | UPDATED: 12:46 EST, 1 October 2013 The people at KFC have revolutionized the take-out container by making one that fits inside your car's cup holder. The KFC Go Cup comes with a choice of five combinations of the restaurant's popular chicken treats, all with a side of potato wedges. KFC says the idea for the ingenious containers came when research showed that people are largely using their cup holders for things other than drinks. World-changing: KFC has introduced the Go Cup, a take-out box with a choice of five combinations of chicken and sides that fits in your car's cup holder. According to KFC, only 33 percent of Americans use the holders for drinks, while 75 percent fill the cup holders with at least something. Those not putting drinks inside are filling the void instead with loose change, phones and electronics, or just trash. What's more, the restaurant formerly known as Kentucky Fried Chicken found that 42 percent of Americans would be more likely to eat in their cars if their food container fit conveniently into their cup holder. For millennials, KFC found that number jumps to 53 percent. Steamy: KFC says it came up with the idea when research showed Americans use cup holders for lots of things besides drinks, including loose coins, phones, and even trash. Seeing an opportunity, KFC came up with Go Cups. The customizable cups come with a piece of boneless Original Recipe chicken, chicken tenders, hot wings, Original Recipe bites, or even a mini chicken sandwich. article_content: Utah is one step closer to once again using firing squads to carry out executions after a highly-contested proposal passed a key vote in the state's Legislature. Before the vote ultimately passed in the Republican-controlled House of Representatives by a 39-34 margin yesterday morning, three missing lawmakers were summoned to break a tie. The state voted to stop allowing prisoners to choose death by firing squad in 2004. Yesterday, Utah lawmakers voted in favor of a proposal that would resurrect the use of firing squads. Rep. Paul Ray and Rep. Curtis Oda celebrated after the vote passed in the state's Legislature. The United States Army used firing squads to execute German prisoners during the Second World War. The proposal still has an uncertain fate in the state's GOP-controlled Senate. Leaders in that chamber have thus far declined to say if they'll support it, and Utah's Republican Gov. Gary Herbert won't say if he's in favor of the measure. Republican Senate President Wayne Niederhauser declined to tell reporters if he'd support it. Rep. Paul Ray is sponsoring the measure. He said: 'It is never easy to talk about taking another life, but in our judicial system we have a means that requires that sometimes. We have to have an option.' He added, according to USA TODAY: 'If we go hanging, if we go to the guillotine, or we go to the firing squad, electric chair, you're still going to have the same circus atmosphere behind it. So is it really going to matter?' The Utah execution chamber was shot up after prisoner Ronnie Lee Gardner was executed by five police officers with .30-caliber Winchester rifles in 2010. Republican Rep. Paul Ray said: 'It is never easy to talk about taking another life, but in our judicial system we have a means that requires that sometimes.' This is the firing squad execution chamber at the Utah State Prison in Draper, Utah. The state voted to stop allowing prisoners to pick death by firing squad in 2004. Lawmakers initially voted 35-35 on the proposal Friday morning. After the tie, the three missing lawmakers were summoned to the floor, where they all voted in favor. During that time, Riverton Republican Rep. Dan McCay switched to vote in favor. A firing squad was last used in the state in 2010 when Ronnie Lee Gardner was executed by five police officers with .30-caliber Winchester rifles. For years, states have used a three-drug combination to execute inmates. European drug makers are now refusing to sell the drugs to prisons and corrections departments out of opposition to the death penalty. Several opponents of the firing squad bill were disappointed by Friday's vote but encouraged it passed on such a slim margin. Anna Brower with the American Civil Liberties Union of Utah said: 'The fact that it was so close in our state is really exciting. I think there are legislators who, while they may have complicated feelings about the death penalty, understand that this particular method is not good advertising for Utah.'

article_content: The Citroen C4 Cactus Flair 1.6 Blue HDi 100 is a charming new addition to the market, set to arrive in October. This French family car emphasizes simplicity, efficiency, and practicality, wrapped in a quirky design. With door grips and fabric trim styled like traditional suitcases, it stands out visually. The Cactus Flair boasts a 1.6-litre HDi four-cylinder turbo diesel engine, reaching 62 mph in 10.7 seconds with a top speed of 114 mph. Its nimble ride, courtesy of 17-inch alloy wheels and electric power steering, makes parking a breeze. While not the fastest, it's perfect for family errands or highway drives. Citroen claims an average fuel efficiency of 83.1 mpg, rising to over 88 mpg during cruising. The distinctive 'Airbumps' absorb minor side impacts, and the innovative roof-mounted airbag frees up dashboard space. Prices start at £12,990 for the 1.2-litre PureTech 75 manual, up to £18,190 for the 1.6-litre e-HDi 92 ETG6. The dashboard is hi-tech and clutter-free, featuring digital controls around a 7-inch touch screen. However, the £20,325 price tag, including extras like a trim pack, sunroof, and parking assist, may seem high for a back-to-basics car. Additionally, there are blind spots, particularly towards the left rear, and some interior plastics feel cheap.

article_content: LOS ANGELES, California (CNN) -- Like all zombie movies, 'Zombieland' has hundreds of zombies doing awful things, such as attacking and eating humans, but you could argue it's not a typical zombie movie. Jesse Eisenberg and Woody Harrelson find themselves battling the undead in 'Zombieland.' Zombie hordes do chase the main characters in a post-apocalyptic world, but the focus is on the comedy's stars, including two Oscar nominees -- Woody Harrelson and Abigail Breslin -- along with Jesse Eisenberg and Emma Stone. (Spoiler alert: A third Oscar nominee makes a remarkable cameo appearance, but this story will avoid spoiling the surprise by naming him.) 'We wanted to make a cool, kick-ass road movie about a dysfunctional family traveling across the country and zombies provide us the antagonists, the threat that our characters need to come together,' said Paul Wernick, who wrote the screenplay with partner Rhett Reese. In fact, Wernick had only seen one zombie film before writing this script. Reese, who is a fan of the genre, kept the story on a track that would feed zombie fans' hunger for blood-and-guts action. 'The zombie genre is so well traveled, there is really no reason to get into it unless we could do it in a fresh, different way,' Reese said. 'We were almost forced to think outside the box to make it an entertaining zombie movie.' 'Zombieland' is set in the United States months after a fast-moving virus begins turning most people into flesh-eating zombies. A handful of survivors come together to fight back. Wernick and Reese literally rewrote the rules for zombie films in this movie. Eisenberg's character is an obsessive-compulsive man who developed 47 rules -- such as 'fasten your seat belt' -- designed to help him survive in Zombieland. While Eisenberg journeys to find his parents, he joins Harrelson, a zombie killer who is searching for the last Hostess Twinkie before its expiration date. Stone and Breslin play sisters who survive on their con artist skills. Their goal is to reach a California amusement park, which they think could be free of zombies. The cross-country trip these four characters share resembles 'National Lampoon's Vacation' -- if written and directed by Quentin Tarantino. Wernick said they wanted to be 'very free-wheeling.' The movie 'gives the audience the thrill of the journey,' he said. 'We wanted to take some wild turns.' 'The rules that we lived by when writing this is in fact that there are no rules,' he said. 'Zombieland' may be to zombies what Tarantino's 'Inglourious Basterds' is to Nazis. Wernick and Reese, who have been close friends since high school, often finish each other's sentences as if they were an old-married couple. 'When we were trying to get 'Zombieland' off the ground back in the early days, we ...' Wernick said. '... assaulted Tarantino at an awards-show, to try to get him to read the script,' Reese said. 'That didn't work out,' Wernick said in conclusion to their joint thought. 'He thought we were zombies coming after him.' 'Zombieland,' directed by Rubin Fleischer, offers many of the same elements as a Tarantino film. '[Tarantino] is all about dialogue, character, irreverence, pop culture and we love all those things over the years,' Reese said. 'We have always been inspired by him.' The writers had to run through a number of actors before finding the person for the 10-minute cameo. Among them was Patrick Swayze, the writers' first choice. Swayze, who died just two weeks before the movie's release, turned down the role because of ill health earlier this year. Also asked: Joe Pesci, Steven Seagal, Jean-Claude Van Damme, Dwayne 'The Rock' Johnson, Matthew McConaughey, Mark Hamill, Kevin Bacon and Sylvester Stallone. They were asked, but either didn't want the role or were not available, according to Wernick and Reese. With just a few days before filming the scenes, they asked Harrelson to look in his cell-phone for names and numbers. He came up with a man who's been an Oscar-nominee and Emmy-winner. And now, he's got a key role in a zombie film.

جیسے 'اپنی سیٹ بیلٹ باندھیں' - جو اسے زومبی لینڈ میں زندہ رہنے میں مدد کرنے کے لیے ڈیزائن کیے گئے ہیں۔ جبکہ آئزنبرگ اپنے والدین کو تلاش کرنے کے لیے سفر کر رہا ہے، وہ ہیرلسن، ایک زومبی قاتل سے شامل ہوتا ہے جو آخری ہوسٹس ٹوینکی کو اس کی میعاد ختم ہونے سے پہلے تلاش کر رہا ہے۔ اسٹون اور بریسلن ان بہنوں کا کردار ادا کر رہے ہیں جو اپنے فریب کار ہنر پر زندہ رہتے ہیں۔ ان کا مقصد کیلیفورنیا کے ایک منورنگی پارک تک پہنچنا ہے، جسے وہ زومبیوں سے پاک سمجھتے ہیں۔ ان چار کرداروں کا یہ ملک بھر کا سفر 'نیشنل لیمپون'س ویکیشن' جیسا لگتا ہے - اگر اسے کوئنٹن ٹارنٹینو نے لکھا اور ہدایت کی ہوتی۔ ویرنک نے کہا کہ وہ 'بالکل فری-ویلنگ' ہونا چاہتے تھے۔ فلم 'اس سفر کا تھرل دیتی ہے،' اس نے کہا۔ 'ہم کچھ جنگلی موڑ لینا چاہتے تھے۔' 'ہمارے لکھنے کے قوانین کے مطابق حقیقت یہ ہے کہ کوئی قوانین نہیں ہیں،' اس نے کہا۔ 'زومبی لینڈ' زومبیوں کے لیے وہ ہے جو ٹارنٹینو کا 'انگلوریس باسٹرڈز' نازیوں کے لیے ہے۔ ویرنک اور ریس، جو ہائی اسکول سے ہی قریبی دوست رہے ہیں، اکثر ایک دوسرے کی جملوں کو ایک پرانے شادی شدہ جوڑے کی طرح مکمل کرتے ہیں۔ 'جب ہم 'زومبی لینڈ' کو ابتدائی دنوں میں اٹھانے کی کوشش کر رہے تھے، ہم ...' ویرنک نے کہا۔ '... ٹارنٹینو پر ایک ایوارڈ شو میں حملہ کیا، اسے اسکرپٹ پڑھنے کی کوشش کی،' ریس نے کہا۔ 'وہ کامیاب نہیں ہوا،' ویرنک نے اپنے مشترکہ خیال کے اختتام پر کہا۔ 'اس نے سوچا کہ ہم زومبی ہیں جو اس کے پیچھے آ رہے ہیں۔' 'زومبی لینڈ،' جس کی ہدایتکاری روبن فلیشر نے کی ہے، ایک ٹارنٹینو فلم کے کئی عناصر فراہم کرتی ہے۔ '[ٹارنٹینو] ڈائیلاگ، کردار، بے ادبی، پاپ ثقافت کے بارے میں ہے اور ہم ان سب چیزوں کو سالوں سے پسند کرتے ہیں،' ریس نے کہا۔ 'ہم ہمیشہ سے ان سے متاثر رہے ہیں۔' لیکھاریوں کو 10 منٹ کے کیمیو کے لیے شخص کی تلاش کے لیے کئی اداکاروں کے ذریعے سے گزرنا پڑا۔ ان میں سے ایک پیٹرک سویزی تھے، جو لیکھاریوں کی پہلی پسند تھے۔ سویزی، جو فلم کی ریلیز سے صرف دو ہفتے پہلے انتقال کر گئے، نے اس سال کے ابتدا میں علالت کی وجہ سے اس کردار کو ٹھکرا دیا۔ دیگر جنہیں پوچھا گیا: جو پیسی، سٹیون سیگل، جین-کلاؤڈ وان ڈیم، ڈوین 'دی راک' جانسن، میتھیو میکونہے، مارک ہیمل، کیون بیکن اور سلویسٹر سٹالون۔ ویرنک اور ریس کے مطابق، انھیں یا تو کردار پسند نہیں آیا یا دستیاب نہیں تھا۔ صرف کچھ دنوں میں ہی سینوں کی فلم بندی سے پہلے، انھوں نے ہیرلسن سے اپنے سیل-فون میں نام اور نمبروں کی تلاش کرنے کو کہا۔ اس نے ایک آدمی کا نام لیا جس نے ایک اوسکر-نامزد اور ایمی-فاتح ہے۔ اور اب، اس کے پاس ایک زومبی فلم میں ایک اہم کردار ہے۔

article_content: In a recent diplomatic flare-up, Indonesia called in the Australian ambassador, Greg Moriarty, to express its displeasure over reports that Australia attempted to eavesdrop on President Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono's phone conversations. The Australian embassy in Jakarta confirmed that Moriarty acknowledged Indonesia's concerns and would relay them back to his government. The controversy stems from revelations by the Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC) and Guardian Australia, which reported that Australian intelligence agencies tracked Yudhoyono's mobile phone for 15 days in August 2009. The reports, based on documents leaked by Edward Snowden, suggest that while the agencies tried to listen in on at least one call, they were unsuccessful due to its short duration. Indonesian presidential spokesman Teuku Faizasyah took to Twitter, urging the Australian government to clarify the matter promptly to mitigate further damage to bilateral relations. 'The damage has been done and now trust must be rebuilt,' he stated in a subsequent tweet. When questioned in parliament about the allegations, Australian Prime Minister Tony Abbott neither confirmed nor denied the reports. He simply noted that all governments engage in intelligence gathering and maintained Australia's policy of not commenting on specific intelligence activities.

article_content: Suzanne Somers, best known for her iconic role in the hit television series 'Three’s Company' and later appearances in 'She’s the Sheriff' and 'Step by Step', has passed away at the age of 76. She died peacefully at her home in the early morning hours of October 15th. Somers had survived an aggressive form of breast cancer for over 23 years. 'Suzanne Somers passed away peacefully at home in the early morning hours of October 15th. She survived an aggressive form of breast cancer for over 23 years,' stated R. Couri Hay, Somers’ longtime publicist, in a statement to People on behalf of the actress’ family. 'Suzanne was surrounded by her loving husband Alan, her son Bruce, and her immediate family,' the statement continued. 'Her family was gathered to celebrate her 77th birthday on October 16th. Instead, they will celebrate her extraordinary life, and want to thank her millions of fans and followers who loved her dearly.' Somers first made a cultural impact as the blonde beauty in a white Thunderbird in George Lucas’ ‘60s hit comedy-drama, 'American Graffiti' (1973). Her big break came in 1977 when she was cast as one of the two female leads in the third pilot for 'Three’s Company'. Somers embodied the 'dumb blonde' stereotype on the show as Chrissy Snow. She starred alongside Joyce DeWitt and John Ritter in the improbable sitcom about three roommates that captivated TV audiences, rising to No. 3 in the national ratings in its 1977-78 debut season. The racy show for its time remained in the Nielsen Top 5 through the beginning of the 1980 season when Somers exited due to a business conflict. She made brief cameos that season and was completely written off the show afterward, replaced by other characters. 'I knew what Chrissy Snow would and would not do,' Somers said in a 2009 interview for the Television Academy Foundation. 'She’d never tell a lie. She’d never steal anybody’s boyfriend. Everything was always absolutely honest with her. And I think that’s what endeared her to the public.' From there, Somers tried a Vegas act and then starred in the syndicated sitcom 'She’s the Sheriff'. In 1991, she regained momentum when she was cast opposite Patrick Duffy in 'Step by Step', a traditional sitcom about blended families. It lasted six seasons on ABC, then moved to CBS for a final season in 1997-98. Acting took a backseat for Somers, who built a multimillion-dollar fitness empire thanks to TV infomercials for the ThighMaster, soon followed by the ButtMaster. She and her husband Alan Hamel amassed a fortune estimated in the hundreds of millions of dollars from these toning products. This was followed by two dozen books on wellness, weight loss, and sex, with Home Shopping Network appearances and her own website providing additional revenue. Show business still played a small role in her life. She co-hosted 'Candid Camera' in 1997 and hosted the Lifetime talk show 'The Suzanne Show' in 2012. She also appeared on 'Dancing with the Stars' in 2015. Her resume includes the 1988 memoir 'Keeping Secrets', later adapted into an ABC TV movie. She wrote a sequel novel and performed a one-woman Broadway show, 'The Blonde in the Thunderbird'. Her film and TV credits include a small part in the Steve McQueen action film 'Bullitt' (1968), roles on 'The Rockford Files', 'Starsky & Hutch', 'The Love Boat', and 'One Day at a Time'. Her movie work included Clint Eastwood’s second Dirty Harry film, 'Magnum Force' (1973), and 'Billy Jack Goes to Washington' (1977). She is survived by her husband and son.

تھنڈربرڈ میں بلونڈ خوبصورتی کے طور پر ڈالا، جو جارج لوکاس کی '60 کی دہائی کی ہٹ کامیڈی ڈراما 'امریکن گرافیٹی' (1973) میں نظر آئی۔ ان کا بڑا بریک 1977 میں آیا جب انھیں 'تھریز کمپنی' کے تیسرے پائلٹ کے لیے دو خواتین سربراہوں میں سے ایک کے طور پر کاسٹ کیا گیا۔ سامرز نے شو میں 'بیوقوف بلونڈ' کی ضمن میں کردار ادا کیا۔ وہ جوائس ڈی وِٹ اور جان رِٹر کے ساتھ تین روم میٹس کے بارے میں ایک غیر معمولی سٹکام میں نظر آئیں جس نے ٹی وی کے شائقین کی توجہ حاصل کی، جس نے اپنے 1977-78 کے ڈیبیو سیزن میں قومی ریٹنگ میں نمبر 3 پر پہنچ گیا۔ اس دور کے لیے جنسی شو نے 1980 کے سیزن کے آغاز تک نیلسن ٹاپ 5 میں رہا جب سامرز نے ایک کاروباری تنازع کی وجہ سے شو چھوڑ دیا۔ اس سیزن میں انھوں نے مختصر کیمیو کیے اور اس کے بعد شو سے پوری طرح نکال دیا گیا، دوسرے کرداروں سے تبدیل کیا گیا۔ 'مجھے پتہ تھا کہ کرسی سنو کیا کرے گی اور کیا نہیں کرے گی،' سامرز نے 2009 میں ٹیلی ویژن اکیڈمی فاؤنڈیشن کے لیے ایک انٹرویو میں کہا۔ 'وہ کبھی جھوٹ نہیں بولے گی۔ وہ کبھی کسی کے بوائے فرینڈ کو نہیں چوری کرے گی۔ ہر چیز ہمیشہ ان کے ساتھ بالکل صاف تھی۔ اور میرا خیال ہے کہ یہی وہ چیز تھی جس نے انھیں عوام میں مقبول بنایا۔' وہاں سے، سامرز نے ایک ویگاس ایکٹ کو آزمایا اور پھر سنڈیکیٹڈ سٹکام 'شی دی شیرف' میں اداکاری کی۔ 1991 میں، انھوں نے دوبارہ زور پکڑا جب انھیں پیٹرک ڈفی کے مقابل 'اسٹیپ بائی اسٹیپ' میں کاسٹ کیا گیا، جو مخلوط خاندانوں کے بارے میں ایک روایتی سٹکام تھا۔ یہ شو شش سیزن تک ای بی سی پر چلا، پھر 1997-98 میں ایک آخری سیزن کے لیے سی بی ایس پر منتقل ہو گیا۔ اداکاری نے سامرز کے لیے پس پردہ رول ادا کیا، جنھوں نے ٹی وی انفومرشلز کی مدد سے ٹائٹ ماسٹر اور پھر بٹ ماسٹر کے لیے ایک کثیر الاقلام فٹنس سلطنت تعمیر کی۔ انھوں نے اور ان کے شوہر الان ہیمل نے ان ٹوننگ پروڈکٹس سے سینکڑوں ملین ڈالر کی دولت جمع کی۔ اس کے بعد درجنوں کتابیں صحت، وزن کم کرنے اور جنس پر آئیں، ہوم شاپنگ نیٹ ورک پر نمودار ہونے اور ان کی اپنی ویب سائٹ سے مزید رقم حاصل ہوئی۔ شو بزنس نے اب بھی ان کی زندگی میں ایک چھوٹا سا کردار ادا کیا۔ انھوں نے 1997 میں 'کینڈڈ کیمرا' کی مشترکہ میزبانی کی اور 2012 میں لائف ٹائم ٹاک شو 'دی سوزان شو' کی میزبانی کی۔ انھوں نے 2015 میں 'ڈانسنگ ود دی اسٹارز' میں بھی شرکت کی۔ ان کے ریزومے میں 1988 کی میموار 'کیپنگ سیکریٹس' شامل ہے، جسے بعد میں ایک ای بی سی ٹی وی مووی میں ڈالا گیا۔ انھوں نے ایک سیکوئل ناول بھی لکھا اور ایک ون وومن براڈوے شو 'دی بلونڈ ان دی تھنڈربرڈ' پرفارم کیا۔ ان کے فلم اور ٹی وی کے کام میں سٹیو میک کوئین ایکشن فلم 'بولٹ' (1968) میں ایک چھوٹا سا کردار، 'دی راکفورڈ فائلز'، 'سٹارسکی اینڈ ہچ'، 'دی لو بوٹ' اور 'ون ڈے ایٹ اے ٹائم' پر کردار شامل ہیں۔ ان کی فلمی کام میں کلنٹ ایسٹ ووڈ کی دوسری ڈرٹی ہیری فلم 'میگنم فورس' (1973) اور 'بلی جیک گوز ٹو واشنگٹن' (1977) شامل ہیں۔ وہ اپنے شوہر اور بیٹے کے ساتھ زندہ ہیں۔
